facts.text: Okotoks has 1,227 businesses in 2022, an 11.2 per cent increase from 1,103 in 2021.
facts.publisher: Alberta Regional Dashboard, Government of Alberta
facts.evidence: Okotoks had 1,227 businesses in 2022, with an 11.2% increase from 1,103 in 2021.

facts.text: Ninety-six per cent of Okotoks businesses have fewer than 50 employees, many of them in retail and construction.
facts.evidence: 96 per cent of the town's businesses have less than 50 employees, many of which are in retail and construction.

facts.text: Industrial employers in Okotoks include Rolco Rollshutters, Burnco Rock Products, McLean Contracting, Taylor Toolworks, Western Tank and Lining and McAsphalt Industries.
facts.evidence: Some of the main industrial employers in Okotoks include Rolco Rollshutters, Burnco Rock Products, McLean Contracting, Taylor Toolworks, Western Tank and Lining, McAsphalt Industries

facts.text: A regional water pipeline for Okotoks and Foothills County, drawing from where the Highwood meets the Bow River, receives a $15.9 million provincial grant.
facts.evidence: A project to help the Town of Okotoks and Foothills County secure a long-term water supply received a provincial grant of $15.9 million. The water pipeline will feed from where the Highwood River meets the Bow River

meta.descriptor: a town about 15 kilometres south of Calgary in the Foothills region
meta.fact: a small-business town where 96 per cent of firms have fewer than 50 employees

overview: Okotoks had 30,405 residents in 2021, up 4.8 per cent from 2016, in 10,476 occupied homes. Water supply limits have constrained the town's growth for more than a decade, which kept its population gains modest.

Almost all local businesses are small, and many work in retail and construction. With a regional water pipeline now funded, growth is set to resume, and businesses that build a strong reputation now will be well placed as new residents arrive.

byService.lead-generation: Okotoks grew a modest 4.8 per cent from 2016 to 2021, so lead generation should focus on winning existing households and referrals rather than relying on newcomers alone.
byService.seo: Okotoks businesses compete with south Calgary for many of the same searches, so local SEO should target the town name and neighbourhoods like Westmount and Cimarron to capture nearby customers.
byService.website-development: In a town dominated by small firms, an Okotoks website that clearly shows reviews, local projects and easy booking can set a business apart from competitors with dated sites.
byService.branding: Branding in Okotoks should emphasise small-town ownership and community ties, since residents of its 10,476 households often choose local businesses over Calgary chains.
